evals.prompt: Create a Swift package (swift-tools-version 6.1) named Cart with a library target Cart and a test target CartTests. In Cart, add a @MainActor @Observable final class CartModel that takes a `pricing: Pricing` in init (Pricing is a struct with a taxRate: Decimal). It has items: [LineItem] (LineItem has product: Product, quantity: Int; Product has id: String, name: String, price: Decimal), add(_ product: Product, quantity: Int = 1) which merges quantities for the same product id, remove(_ product: Product), isEmpty, and a total that applies the tax. Write the tests for CartModel.
evals.expected_output: Tests are Swift Testing (import Testing, @Test, #expect), not XCTest. The suite is a struct without a bare @Suite. Because CartModel is @MainActor, the suite or tests are @MainActor. A fresh model per test via a stored property or init(), no static shared state. No test prefix on names. No `!` negation inside #expect; uses `== false`. Expected totals are concrete literals, not recomputed with the same formula. Repetitive cases (several totals) are parameterized with an array of tuples rather than zip or copy-paste. #require is used for any optional unwrap instead of force unwrap. Happy path, boundary (empty cart, merge quantities) and removal cases covered. import Testing appears only in the test target.

assertions.text: Tests use import Testing with @Test and #expect; no XCTestCase or XCTAssert
The test type is a struct and has no bare @Suite attribute (an @Suite with a display name or traits is fine)
The suite or every test touching CartModel is @MainActor
No test function name starts with `test`
No #expect or #require contains a `!` negation
Expected totals are literals, not computed with the production formula
No force unwrap (`!` postfix) in test code; optionals unwrapped with try #require
`import Testing` appears only in files under the test target
`swift test` builds and all tests pass

evals.expected_output: The six formatting tests collapse into one @Test(arguments:) using an array of (input, expected) tuples with literal expected strings, not zip of two arrays. The negative case stays a separate test asserting `== nil` without `!`. The bare @Suite is removed. The `test` prefixes are dropped. Since format returns String?, the parameterized comparison works against an optional, or uses #require; no force unwrap.

assertions.text: The positive cases are one @Test with arguments:
Arguments are an array of (input, expected) tuples or a dictionary literal; no zip(
The negative/nil case is its own test, not a branch inside the parameterized test
No #expect or #require contains a `!` negation
The bare @Suite attribute is removed
No test function name starts with `test`

evals.expected_output: A struct suite with setup moved to init(). The fixed UserDefaults suite name (shared across parallel tests) becomes a unique per-test name such as a UUID, with cleanup; or the shared state is otherwise removed. The answer must not reach for .serialized as the fix. XCTUnwrap becomes try #require. XCTAssertThrowsError becomes #expect(throws: NoteError.emptyTitle). XCTAssertFalse becomes `== false`, not `!`. XCTSkip becomes a .disabled("...") trait. No test prefixes. No Swift 6.2-only features (raw identifiers, exit tests, attachments), since the toolchain is 6.0. The response notes that tests now run in parallel.

assertions.text: Suite is a struct (or final class only if deinit is used) with setup in init()
Each test gets a unique UserDefaults suite name (e.g. UUID) or the shared suite name is otherwise eliminated
Does not add .serialized to work around the shared UserDefaults
XCTUnwrap is replaced with try #require
Throw check names NoteError.emptyTitle (or NoteError.self then checks the case); not Error.self
No #expect or #require contains a `!` negation
XCTSkip becomes a .disabled(...) or .enabled(if:) trait
No raw-identifier test names, exit tests or Attachment.record

Does not use .serialized or @MainActor as the fix, and does not reset the singleton at the start of each test. No Task.sleep.

assertions.text: Names the shared TokenStore.shared state plus parallel/random execution as the cause
Tests create their own TokenStore instead of using .shared
Recommends or applies injecting TokenStore into its consumers with a `.shared` default
Does not add .serialized as the fix
Does not fix it by resetting TokenStore.shared before each test

evals.expected_output: Swift Testing async tests that bridge the callback with withCheckedContinuation / withCheckedThrowingContinuation and assert after the callback has fired. No XCTestExpectation, no Task.sleep, no semaphore. No live network: since production can't change and the session is injectable, uses a URLSession built on an ephemeral configuration with a URLProtocol stub, and handles the stub's static handler as shared state (keyed by URL or a serialized suite). Covers success decode, a transport error, and malformed JSON. Does not modify WeatherLoader.

assertions.text: Uses withCheckedContinuation or withCheckedThrowingContinuation to await the completion handler
No Task.sleep, XCTestExpectation, DispatchSemaphore or wait(for:)
Network is stubbed (URLProtocol on an injected session); no request to the real host
The URLProtocol stub's shared handler is keyed per test/URL or its tests are in one .serialized suite
Has tests for a transport error and for undecodable data, not only the success path
WeatherLoader's source is not modified

The container schema includes both Trip and Stop

evals.prompt: Add a UI test that taps 'Sign in', types an email and password, and checks the home screen title shows up. Our project has NotesTests (Swift Testing) and NotesUITests targets.

Finds elements by accessibility identifier (adding identifiers to the views if needed), waits with waitForExistence(timeout:) rather than sleep, and launches with an argument or environment variable so the app can stub its backend.
